findings.diagnosis: The shipped chapter runs from the funding paradox straight to the research lineages. The two convergent findings, that durable transformation has been capitalized through patient endowment or mission-compatible revenue, and that conventional investment capital has consistently either compromised the commitments or failed to reach scale, are the empirical basis for Chapter Eight's entire list of compatible capital forms. Chapter Eight in the shipped text therefore asserts its conclusions with the evidence section removed.

evidence.baseline: This finding is uncomfortable for founders in the contemporary technology environment, where venture capital is the most available and culturally legible form of early-stage institutional funding. The discomfort is appropriate. ... venture capital is optimized for platform logic, and attempting to build protocol infrastructure on venture capital generates the predictable pressure toward platform conversion.

findings.diagnosis: This is the volume's only direct address to the reader most likely to be building something: a founder who has already raised or intends to. The discomfort is appropriate is a two word refusal to soften, and the platform and protocol link is the thread back to Volume III that makes the finding constitutional rather than merely prudential.

reasoning.note: R-PUNCT-STRUCT. Four em dashes. Three were parenthetical appositives defining a capital model and became comma pairs. One introduced a specification and became a colon.
The whole section: both convergent findings, the university endowment and cooperative ownership examples, the consistency argument, and the address to founders in the technology environment.
The section's headings and position are unchanged. Only the body was absent.

openQuestions: The restored claim that institutions attempting to fund transformational work through conventional investment capital have with remarkable consistency either compromised or failed is a strong empirical generalization with no source. It is the section's central finding. CTD-0078 reaches it directly.

The volume-04 voice card was prepared by the same pass that produced the shipped text, and its exemplar anchors and protected lines quote that text rather than the baseline. The card records `Author approved: pending tone, strategy, heading, and overcompression review`. The restoration keeps every line the card protects and otherwise follows the baseline, which means card and source now diverge in wording the card does not name. R-VOICE-BIND requires that the disagreement be raised rather than settled here: the card should be re-derived from whichever text the author approves.

Structural labels were frozen for this pass and none was touched. Every markdown heading, every standalone bold display line, every chapter label, and every all-capital display line is byte identical to its pre-edit state, in the same order, with the same blank-line separators on both sides. A label determines a section id, a section id is a public route, and `publishing/continuity/section-lineage.json` already records this volume's renames and resolves the historical routes. Changing one is a continuity decision and not an editorial one. Only the running prose between labels was restored. Where a baseline label names its section better than the current one, the cost is recorded here and the label is left alone.

regenerationTest.purpose: The rules must reproduce the section from the baseline without consulting the shipped text.
regenerationTest.method: Derived from the immutable baseline applying editorial/method/standard.md, the corpus voice card, the volume-04 voice card, and the debt ledger under R-LEDGER-WINS.
regenerationTest.conclusion: No new rule required. This is the first section in the volume whose body was removed outright rather than reduced, and the damage report's minus sixty-nine percent understates it because the research lineages and open questions that follow were counted inside the section. Word count is not a reliable detector of wholesale removal when display blocks survive.

audits.auditor: editorial-agent, generation 1 of the twenty-rule re-render lane
audits.scope: Full re-read of the current section against the immutable baseline under all twenty rules. The original record was derived under the thirteen-rule index; this audit adds the substitution count and the later rules: R-LEDGER-WINS-COROLLARY, R-CORRECTION-SCOPE, R-CANON-DELETION-RECORD, R-PAIRED-DELETION, R-CAUTIOUS-HALF, R-SUBSTITUTION-CREDIT, and R-REFRAIN-COST.

substitutionTest.rule: R-CAUTIOUS-HALF, substitution form, run as standing procedure before any pairing test
substitutionTest.method: Normalize both texts, strip markup, split into sentences of three or more words, count baseline sentences appearing verbatim in the current section.
substitutionTest.note: Well above zero, so the section is a restoration, not a substitution, and the pairing test applies. Verbatim survival understates fidelity here: every R-PUNCT-STRUCT repair and recorded bounding changes the sentence it lands in, so the non-surviving remainder was read against the diff and attributed rather than assumed lost.

audits.checked: R-CAUTIOUS-HALF: both convergent findings keep their committing form beside the restored consistency argument, and the second open question keeps the empirical hedge the baseline gave it. R-PAIRED-DELETION: patient endowment, cooperative ownership, and community bonds were swept; the same triad recurs in the two open questions and in Capital Patient Enough, all ends aligned. Citations re-verified intact through the punctuation repairs: Kelly 2001 and 2012, Mazzucato 2013 and 2021, Alperovitz 2005 and 2013, and the Institute for Local Self-Reliance. R-CORRECTION-SCOPE: one factual correction found and recorded below. R-SUBSTITUTION-CREDIT: nothing kept from the shipped pass beyond the display labels, no credit owed, stated explicitly. R-TENSE, R-DEIXIS, R-NEGATION-STACK, R-REFRAIN-COST, R-LEDGER-WINS-COROLLARY: nothing fires.
audits.conclusion: The restoration holds under the full twenty-rule index. Twenty-one of thirty baseline sentences survive verbatim; the remainder are the four recorded punctuation repairs, the renamed display labels held under the structural rule, and the now-sourced name correction. No prose change required.
corrections: A factual correction the restoration made silently is now recorded with its source, as section 9 of the standard requires. The baseline attributes The Entrepreneurial State (2013) and Mission Economy (2021) to Michael Mazzucato while continuing Her analysis, an internal inconsistency; the manuscript reads Mariana Mazzucato, which is correct. Source: both works are by Mariana Mazzucato, the economist at University College London; The Entrepreneurial State, Anthem Press, 2013, and Mission Economy, Allen Lane, 2021. The baseline's pronoun already agreed with the correction.
One small divergence attributed: in the funding paradox chapter stands as in the funding paradox, a 4.23 trim of a self-referential label, claim unchanged.
